report:
Reviewed the complete project_isolation claim and all nine ordinary implementation associations and five ordinary tests; there are no TODO/N/A entries. Requirements are per-invocation materialization of the supplied source, isolation from caller directory and enclosing workspace default selection, deterministic logical paths, ordinary-library compilation, cfg(test) disabled, and no Cargo features inherited from the enclosing test. compile/mod.rs validates relative fixture paths, fixes src/lib.rs, creates a fresh tempfile directory, writes the supplied bytes and a minimal Cargo package with its own [workspace], and opens that exact directory. rustc.rs explicitly changes the subprocess directory to that project and compiles src/lib.rs with --crate-type lib and no --test or feature flags. metadata.rs runs Cargo metadata in the supplied directory, selects the library target from that workspace, reads its enabled features, and obtains ordinary rustc target cfgs; the generated manifest has no features or dependencies. driver.rs builds a fresh host/database, loads source paths relative to the selected source directory, and installs the selected cfgs. db.rs stores those cfg inputs independently in each fresh database. parse/mod.rs filters disabled items before constructing them; parse/attrs.rs evaluates cfg predicates against those inputs, including all/any/not and feature strings; parse/items.rs applies the same filtering to associated items. observe.rs restores the fixture-relative src/ path prefix for observations and diagnostics. Added associations for metadata.rs, parse/items.rs, and observe.rs because those files are essential to this claim.

The associated cold_queries_are_stable_across_isolated_projects test compares two independently prepared query streams, requires executed body work, and excludes temporary paths and unstable IDs. configuration_selects_items_before_checking asserts successful compilation of an included item gated by not(test)/not(feature), an excluded missing module, and an impl with an invalid cfg(test) method and a valid not(test) method. ordinary_library_disables_test_configuration and ordinary_library_disables_unselected_features each place a real type error behind the disabled predicate; macro preparation runs both compilers and rejects unmatched errors, so successful execution meaningfully asserts exclusion. The added fixtures_ignore_caller_directory_and_workspace_defaults subprocess test runs the same visible fixture assertions from both an unrelated directory and an enclosing workspace whose default member contains compile_error!. It requires child success and exactly one passed test, preventing an empty filtered run from passing. Each child checks two fixtures with the same filename/function name but different supplied literals and return types, with explicit fixture-relative src/lib.rs observation snapshots. The parent uses subprocess current_dir instead of changing the test process directory and removes UPDATE_EXPECT in children. This closes the previous cwd/default-members and distinct-source coverage gaps without changing production behavior.

Commands actually executed: cargo fmt; cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test review_fixture fixtures_ignore_caller_directory_and_workspace_defaults -- --exact (one passed, including both child directory scenarios); cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test review_fixture ordinary_library_ -- --nocapture (two passed); cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test compile_tests configuration_selects_items_before_checking -- --exact (one passed); cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib cold_queries_are_stable_across_isolated_projects (one passed). Existing compiler warnings were emitted. This assessment distinguishes those executed focused tests from source inspection; workspace build and central delegated quality checks remain coordinator responsibilities. Re-started and inspected fresh inputs after adding tests/associations, and captured the review policy with review read. No behavioral violation remains identified and every claim aspect has implementation and assertion coverage.
